# Fakturama Image-to-Cash Automation

## Objective

Build a system that turns a single order image into a fully saved, verified Order and linked Invoice inside Fakturama — extracting the source data, resolving or creating the Debtor and Product master records, and applying the correct payment status, without relying on hardcoded coordinates or a fixed UI layout.

  

This task is intentionally larger than the timebox. We don't expect a fully complete flow — do as much as you can in the time and be ready to talk through what's left. That tradeoff is close to real work here: the scope is usually bigger than the clock.

  

# Part 1: Design Doc

  

Timebox: Up to 90 minutes Deliverable: 1–4 pages, no code

  

Context

  

- Fakturama is a desktop invoicing/accounting application. You'll receive a single order image (for example, a scanned or photographed purchase order) as the only input.
    
- Download Fakturama at https://www.fakturama.info/download/. 
    
- The system must extract structured data from that image, then use Fakturama's UI to resolve or create the Debtor, resolve or create each Product (and its VAT rate), build the Order, generate a linked Invoice, and apply the extracted payment status — verifying each step before moving to the next.
    
- This part is intentionally open in how you'd locate and interact with Fakturama's UI controls and how you'd extract and validate the source data. There's no single correct answer.
    

  

Your Task

  

Write a short design document describing how you would build this system. No code required for this step. You may structure the document however you like. Examples of topics include:

  

- Control-discovery / grounding strategy: how you'd reliably find and interact with Fakturama's UI elements
    
- Image-extraction strategy
    
- Tradeoffs of your approach
    

  

# Part 2: Implementation

  

Timebox: Up to 5 hours — do as much as you can Deliverable: Git repo

  

Context

  

Based on the design document you just completed, you'll now implement the Fakturama Image-to-Cash automation: one continuous Order-first flow from a supplied order image through a saved, verified Invoice. Note anything you skipped in your README and the written questions below.

  

Required implementation approach

  

- Use Microsoft UI Automation (UIA), OCR, and/or LLMs
    

  

Core Task

  

Implement one continuous Order-first flow from a supplied order image. Extract the source data, open a New Order, and use the Order's Debtor and Product selectors as the existence checks. Create missing master data only when an exact selection is unavailable, then return to the same open Order. Complete the Order, create its linked Invoice, apply the extracted payment status, and verify the saved records. Screenshots below are UI references; the Product procedure is shown for one line and repeats for every additional item.

  

## 1. Extract the image and open a New Order

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

1.1. Use OCR and/or an LLM as needed to extract and normalize the supplied order image. 

1.2. Extract the Order Date and External Reference; Debtor company, contact, alias, addresses, and payment data; and every item SKU, description, quantity, unit net price, VAT percentage, discount, and source total. 

  

Open the Order first

  

1.3. Click Order in the top toolbar and wait for the New Order editor. 

1.4. Leave the automatically proposed No. unchanged. 

1.5. Set Date to the extracted Order Date. 

1.6. Enter the extracted External Reference in Cust.Ref. 

1.7. Set the document price mode to Net and keep VAT as With VAT. 

1.8. Keep this New Order tab open while resolving a missing Debtor, payment method, VAT rate, or Product.

  

## 2. Select or create the Debtor

  

Try to select the Debtor from the Order

  

2.1. Click the upper existing-contact icon beside Addresses. Do not click the lower green + icon, which starts a new Debtor. 

2.2. In Select the address, search using the extracted Company or customer name and wait for the list to stabilize. 

2.3. Treat a Debtor as an exact match only when the visible Company, First Name, Name, ZIP, and City match the extracted values. If one exact row appears, select it and click OK. If results are conflicting or ambiguous, stop for manual review. If no exact row appears, click Cancel and continue with the creation branch below. See Figure 1.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 1. Address selector used to find and select an existing Debtor from the open Order.

  

2.4. When an existing Debtor is selected, confirm that the populated Invoice address and Delivery address match the source image, then continue to Product selection.

  
  

2.5. Keep the Order tab open, click New Contact in the left New panel, and wait for the New Debtor editor. 

2.6. Leave Fakturama's proposed Customer ID unchanged. Enter the extracted Company, First Name, and Last Name; leave Salutation as --- when none is supplied. 

2.7. On Addresses > Main address, enter the billing Street, ZIP, City, Country, E-Mail, and Telephone. Fill additional name, Address specification, or district only when the source supplies those values. 

2.8. Assign the Main address the Invoice address role. If billing and delivery are identical, also assign the Delivery address role and do not create another address. See Figure 2.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 2. Main address completed and assigned the Invoice address role.

  

2.9. Open Miscellaneous. Enter Alias name, set Discount to 0%, and set Net or Gross to Net. 

2.10. Open Payment and select the exact Payment Method extracted from the image. If it is unavailable, keep the Debtor editor open and create it with the following steps. 

2.10.1. Open Data > terms of payment and search the exact Payment Method. 

2.10.2. If one unambiguous exact Payment Method already exists, return to the Debtor editor, select it, and skip the remaining payment-creation substeps. If multiple exact rows or a conflicting definition appears, stop for manual review. If no exact row exists, click the green + control at the upper-right of the list. 

2.10.3. Set Name and Description to the exact Payment Method and leave Account blank. 

2.10.4. Set the payment-code dropdown using this mapping: Bank Transfer = Credit transfer; Credit Card = Credit card; SEPA Direct Debit = SEPA direct debit. 

2.10.5. Set Cash discount, Discount Days, and Net Days to 0. Leave Text 'unpaid', Text 'deposit', and Text 'paid' blank, and do not click Set as standard. 

2.10.6. Click the toolbar Save control once, return to the open Debtor editor, and select the new Payment Method. See Figure 4.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 4. Conditional Bank Transfer setup using the Credit transfer payment code.

  

2.11. Save the Debtor once. 

2.12. Return to the still-open Order, reopen Select the address, search again, select the newly saved Debtor, and click OK. 

2.13. Confirm that the Invoice address/Delivery address now populate correctly. Successful selection from the Order confirms that the new Debtor was saved.

  

## 3. Select or create each Product

  

3.1. Run this complete selection branch for every extracted item row, in source order.

  

Try to select the Product from the Order

  

3.2. Click the upper Product-selection icon beside the Items table. Do not use the green + control. 

3.3. In Select a product, search the exact extracted SKU. If one exact Product appears, select it and click OK. If results conflict, stop for manual review. If no exact SKU appears, click Cancel and use the creation branch below. See Figure 5.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 5. Product selector used to find an exact SKU from the open Order.

  

3.4. Keep the Order tab open. Before opening New product, open Data > VATs and search for the exact required name, such as VAT 19%. 

3.5. Reuse one exact VAT row only when its Name matches VAT followed by the extracted percentage, its Value matches that percentage, and VAT code (E-Invoice) is S (Standard rate). If any setting conflicts, stop for manual review. 

3.6. If the VAT is missing, click the green + control and set Name and Description to VAT followed by the percentage, keep VAT code (E-Invoice) as S (Standard rate), set Value to the percentage, and leave the displayed Standard VAT unchanged. Save once. See Figure 6.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 6. Conditional VAT 19% setup with the Standard rate code and 19% value.

  

3.7. Click New product only after the required VAT exists, so it is available in the Product VAT dropdown. 

3.8. Set Item Number to the extracted SKU and set both Name and Description to the extracted item description. 

3.9. Calculate Price (gross) as Unit net price x (1 + VAT percentage / 100), rounded to two decimal places. Do not apply the transaction-line discount to this Product master price. 

3.10. Set cost price (net) to 0.00, select the exact VAT, and set Stock to 0.00. Leave Category, GTIN, supplier code, allowance, Product Picture, and user defined field 1 blank or unchanged. See Figure 7.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 7. Conditional Product creation with the calculated gross price and required VAT selected.

  

3.11. Click the toolbar Save control once. 

3.12. Return to the still-open Order, reopen Select a product, search the exact SKU, select the newly saved Product, and click OK. If it does not appear, stop for manual review.

  

Complete the selected item line

  

3.13. Set Qty. to the extracted quantity. 

3.14. Set or confirm U.Price equals the extracted Unit net price and VAT equals the extracted percentage. 

3.15. Set the line Discount to the extracted item discount. 

3.16. Confirm line Price equals quantity x unit net price x (1 - discount / 100). 3.17. Repeat Product selection and line completion for every remaining source item.

  

## 4. Complete and save the Order

  

4.1. Confirm the selected Debtor addresses and every Product line match the extracted image. 

4.2. Keep the overall Discount at 0% and Shipping at Free of shipping costs / 0.00 unless the image supplies corresponding order-level values. 

4.3. Confirm Total Net, VAT, and Total match the source totals. 

4.4. Click the toolbar Save control once. 

4.5. Open Data > Documents and confirm one Order row with the generated number, expected Date and Cust.Ref., open state, and Total. See Figure 8.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 8. Illustrative saved single-line Order with its reference, totals, open state, and follow-up actions.

  

4.6. From the saved Order's Create a follow-up document area, click Invoice. Do not use the Invoice button in the top toolbar because the follow-up action preserves the Order relationship. 

4.7. Wait for the linked New Invoice editor, then continue to the final stage.

  

## 5. Complete and verify the linked Invoice

  

5.1. Leave the automatically proposed Invoice No., Invoice Date, and Service date unchanged. Confirm Cust.Ref., Invoice address, Delivery address, Order Date, VAT mode, item lines, and totals were copied from the Order. See Figure 9.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 9. Illustrative linked single-line Invoice populated from the saved Order.

  

5.2. Set or confirm the Invoice payment method equals the Payment Method extracted from the image. If the required method is not available, stop for manual review. 

5.3. If Paid Status is PAID, select paid, set the payment date to the extracted Payment Date, and set Value to the full Invoice Total. If the status is not PAID, leave paid clear and do not invent a date or value. 

5.4. Click the toolbar Save control once. 

5.5. Open Data > Documents and confirm the Invoice row has the expected state and Total while the source Order remains open with the same Cust.Ref. and Total. See Figure 10.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 10. Illustrative final verification of a paid single-line Invoice and its open source Order.

  

5.6. Reopen the Invoice only if needed to confirm the persisted payment method, paid state, payment date, and Value. 

5.7. The flow ends after this verification. Do not create a Delivery, Correction, or Dunning document.

- [ ] Setup instructions: dependencies and how to run the automation against Fakturama
